text: Two forty-seven A.M., Eastern. No engineer is awake.
But fourteen AI agents are changing your network.
From New York to Vancouver, your teams have handed the network to AI agents.
BGP, SD-WAN, firewalls, patching, even incident response.
Twelve hundred changes in one hour. Forty-one reviewed by a human.
So who is watching the agents?
Machine-speed change needs machine-speed observability.
IBM SevOne. Observability, for the age of agentic AI.
Use case one: observe.
SevOne collects SNMP, flow, telemetry, logs and cloud metrics, across the U.S. and Canada, into one real-time view.
And every change an agent makes is tied to its identity, the device it touched, and the effect it had.
Use case two: anticipate.
At one-twelve, a Devin agent changed an SD-WAN policy. Nothing broke.
But SevOne sees the Ashburn to Dallas MPLS link drifting above baseline, and forecasts a breach at eight-forty, before the opening bell.
With the cause, the users at risk, and the fix.
Use case three: prevent.
A Claude Code agent plans to upgrade both core routers at once.
SevOne's pre-flight finds a degraded backup path, and fourteen sites at risk.
The change is held for a human.
The agent re-plans a safe, rolling upgrade.
SevOne's live data becomes the guardrail.
Use case four: react.
A Cursor agent pushes a new WAF rule.
Checkout latency jumps eleven times. SevOne flags it in eight seconds.
It links the anomaly to the change, and the change to the agent, then triggers a rollback through watsonx Orchestrate.
Resolved in forty-seven seconds. Nobody paged at three A.M.
Use case five: control.
Every agent change, attributed. Thirty-seven risky changes, held. And a safe-change score for every agent, based on what it actually did to your network.
That's real control. In real time.
Your AI agents act at machine speed.
SevOne observes at machine speed.
IBM SevOne. See everything. Control everything.
